A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UALIGN. All 20 pages of v1 and 23 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original QA experiments, reward-model ablations, uncertainty-estimation comparisons, and sampling-number sensitivity results.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds original confidence-distribution measurements and dataset-construction and inference timings.

M1.justification: The sampling procedure, uncertainty estimators, reward model, and PPO objective remain unchanged. Appendix B clarifies frozen auxiliary models and shared-base LoRA inference without establishing a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use TriviaQA, SciQ, NQ-Open, English-language LSQA, and TruthfulQA for the ITI baseline. The added timing studies retain existing QA coverage; testing a larger model does not introduce a new task or domain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Table 1, the reward-model ablations, and the uncertainty-estimation comparisons. The new inference-time comparison reuses vanilla ICL, without introducing or revising a comparison method.

E3.justification: New timing protocols evaluate 10,000 QA samples with Llama-3-8B and 70B at four sampling counts on four A100-40GB GPUs, plus inference on a single A100. These supplement the unchanged benchmark splits, training settings, and accuracy evaluation.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 and Appendix B add substantial analyses of construction cost, model-scale feasibility, and inference overhead. Appendix B.1 also compares confidence distributions before and after UALIGN training to examine the justification for freezing uncertainty models. These extend the original component and sampling-number analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the reported performance. V2 introduces no new statistical uncertainty-reporting practice; its confidence distributions describe model behavior.

E6.justification: V2 adds confidence-bin counts in Table 4 and substantial runtime evidence in Tables 5–6. At K=10, sampling takes 25 minutes for 8B and 2 hours 12 minutes for 70B; TriviaQA inference takes 58 minutes for ICL versus 66 for UALIGN. Existing Tables 1–2, AUROC results, and sampling-performance curves remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The method equations and existing appendix mathematics are retained. Appendix D.1 writes explicit formulas for the already stated precision and truthfulness definitions; it adds explanation rather than new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about explicitly using uncertainty estimates for factuality alignment, improved reliability, and generalization. Added efficiency evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations connecting limited confidence shifts to frozen uncertainty models and short answers to affordable sampling. It softens the computational-resource limitation by discussing acceleration, and adds a rationale for combining precision with truthfulness. Existing factuality interpretations and task-expansion limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly documents auxiliary-model freezing, shared-base LoRA inference, two-token uncertainty outputs, parameter overhead, and use of vLLM/bitsandbytes. The ethical statement identifies three expert evaluators for the existing human check. Core hyperparameters and the code-access disclosure remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 connects UALIGN to test-time scaling and reinforced self-training through Snell et al. and Gulcehre et al., and adds several knowledge-boundary, hallucination, and safety citations. The main research positioning remains intact; the Self-DC publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization are retained. V2 adds a cost-analysis section, a method-supplement appendix, metric subsections, and an ethical statement, alongside localized wording, cross-reference, author-block, and acknowledgment edits.

P2.justification: Figure 6 gains a timing panel beside the retained performance curves. Four compact tables present confidence distributions, construction timings, inference timings, and answer categories. Existing figures are otherwise preserved, with some resizing and relocation; the overall layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: V2 makes computational practicality and implementation easier to assess through measured costs and clearer model-update and inference details, improving on v1's largely qualitative cost discussion. The gains are limited: core performance evidence is unchanged, acceleration and quantization configurations remain underspecified, and new Table 7 incorrectly gives UC and UI the same description.
